Variable: A storage place for a value. You assign a value (e.g. name = "Python") and can use it later.
Variables: Storage places for values. You assign values and can use them later.
Function: A reusable block of code. You define it with def and call it with ().
Functions: Reusable blocks of code. You define them with def and call them with ().
List: Stores multiple values. You access them by index (e.g. animals[0]).
Lists: Store multiple values. You access them by index (e.g. animals[0]).
Dictionary: Stores key-value pairs. You access values with their key.
Dictionaries: Store key-value pairs. You access values with their key.
Index: The position of an item in a list. The first entry has index 0.
Loop: Repeats code multiple times. With for you can iterate over a list, for example.
Loops: Repeat code multiple times. With for you can iterate over a list, for example.
Condition: A check that can be true or false. With if you only run code when the condition is true.
Conditions: Checks that can be true or false. With if you only run code when the condition is true.
Data type: The kind of a value: int (whole number), float (decimal number), str (text), bool (true/false).
Data types: The kinds of values: int, float, str, bool. Use type() to check the type.
String: A piece of text in Python. Written in quotation marks, e.g. "Hello".
Strings: Pieces of text in Python. Written in quotation marks.
f-String: A formatted string. With f"Hello {name}" you embed variables into text.
f-Strings: Formatted strings. With f"...{variable}..." you embed variables into text.
Comment: A note in the code. You write comments with # – Python ignores them.
Comments: Notes in the code. You write them with # – Python ignores them.
Key: In a dictionary, the entry you use to retrieve the associated value.
Value: What is stored in a variable or a dictionary entry.
